open_points.subject: R0-91 blocking scope
open_points.text: Whether any value it holds — a customer's contact or fiscal data, an object's address — must be blocked after erasure rather than erased is a question for the legal review of the governance
open_points.question: Which Registry values, if any, must enter blocking instead of erasure, for how long, and what operations and final destruction apply to each?
options: Registry always erases every value
Specified values enter an unreadable blocked state and are later destroyed
Blocked values are moved to a named system outside Registry
open_points.default_guess: Keep the stated interim behavior: Registry erases every value until a new owner decision changes it.

witness.initial: A retention period has lapsed for a customer with contact and fiscal data.
events: The owner invokes erasure.
The legal review later concludes that fiscal data required blocking.
outcomes: Registry irreversibly erases the fiscal data.
Registry preserves the fiscal data in an unreadable blocked state until liabilities lapse.
witness.observer: The owner and a competent authority requesting the retained data

open_points.subject: R0-92 trace correlation
open_points.text: Whether Kernel writes the key it gives as that request id into its trace record, so that a room or pointer leads to exactly one node execution, is Kernel's to state in its case; until it does, the link is one-directional.
open_points.question: Must every Kernel trace record contain Registry's request id, what uniqueness scope applies to it, and which operation can follow a Registry room or pointer to the matching node execution?
options: Require the request id in exactly one Kernel node trace
Allow several node traces for one request id and define the canonical match
Keep no usable Registry-to-trace lookup
open_points.default_guess: Require one trace record per executed Registry request id and make it searchable by that id.

witness.initial: An agent-created room exists with request id R, and Kernel has trace records for the run.
events: The owner investigates who created the room.
The owner searches Kernel's trace using R.
outcomes: Exactly one node execution is found.
No trace can be found from R because Kernel did not record it.

open_points.subject: R0-93 machine-readable subject copy
open_points.text: The machine-readable copy is the owner's, assembled from those reads.
open_points.question: What exact data belongs in the copy, which values count as data provided by the customer, what schema and format are used, and how are erased, restricted, archived and issued-document data represented?
options: A specified JSON schema containing all Registry data about the customer
A JSON serialization of the listed Registry reads
An owner-selected subset of the read results
open_points.default_guess: Produce versioned JSON containing the customer record and every linked project, object, room and artifact pointer, with explicit absent and erased markers.

witness.initial: A customer has contact data, one active project, one archived project and artifact pointers.
events: The customer requests the data they provided in machine-readable form.
The owner assembles a download from Registry reads.
outcomes: The download contains all linked projects, rooms and pointers.
The download contains only the Customer record because the remaining records are treated as project data rather than customer-provided data.

open_points.subject: R0-93 requester verification
open_points.text: A customer may ask what Registry holds about them, for a copy, for the data they provided in a machine-readable form, or for its erasure
open_points.question: How does the owner establish that the requester is the data subject or an authorised representative before disclosing or erasing Registry data?
options: Verify through a recorded governance procedure using existing contact details
Require an authenticated customer-channel request
Leave identity verification to the owner's case-by-case judgement
open_points.default_guess: Use a documented identity-verification procedure outside Registry and record its successful completion before acting.

open_points.subject: R0-93 data held by other services
open_points.text: What other services hold about the customer is answered from those services.
open_points.question: Which services must be queried, by whom, through which actions, and how are their results combined with Registry's answer?
options: The owner queries every service named in the processing record and assembles one response
Each service answers the customer separately
Only Registry data is included unless the customer names another service
open_points.default_guess: The owner queries every service listed in the governance inventory and assembles one coordinated response.

open_points.subject: R0-93 proposed review page and download
open_points.text: A read-only owner operation that gathers a customer with every project naming it, as one page and a JSON download, is a candidate change once the first release is assembled; adopting it is a new owner decision here.
open_points.question: Is this operation part of the product, and if so what triggers its delivery and what exact page and JSON contract does it provide?
options: Adopt it for the first release
Adopt it in a specifically identified later release
Do not add it; retain manual assembly
open_points.default_guess: Do not treat it as promised until a new owner decision adopts a concrete contract.

open_points.subject: R0-94 retention review page delivery
open_points.text: After the first release is assembled, it gains a read-only review page in the owner interface
open_points.question: What event precisely means the first release is assembled, in which release must the page exist, and what happens if that release is deployed before the page is designed?
options: The page is mandatory in the first production release
The page is mandatory in the next release after first production
The page remains only a candidate pending another owner decision
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as mandatory in the next release after the initial production release.

open_points.subject: R0-94 configurable retention periods
open_points.text: the customers whose relationship ended, and the archived projects archived, longer ago than periods the owner sets in the configuration from the schedule
open_points.question: What configuration fields and units define each period, which data kind each applies to, what defaults and validation apply, and when configuration changes take effect?
options: Separate validated periods for customers, projects and audit entries
One common retention period for all review-page items
A schedule supplied as a versioned external policy document
open_points.default_guess: Define separate nonnegative day-based periods for customer relationships and archived projects, validated at startup and effective after restart.

witness.initial: A relationship ended two years ago and its project was archived three years ago.
events: The owner configures a one-year customer period and a five-year project period.
The owner opens the review page.
outcomes: The customer is due but the project is not.
Both are treated as one item and shown or hidden using a single inferred period.
witness.observer: The owner using the retention review

open_points.subject: R0-94 blocking mechanism
open_points.text: If the legal review answers that some value must be blocked, blocking enters the same change, as one mechanism with the review page. The design of both is decided then, by a new owner decision here.
open_points.question: Is the review page allowed to ship without blocking, and what state model, actions, reads, destruction rule and migration apply if blocking is required?
options: Ship the review page independently and add blocking only after a legal decision
Delay the page until the legal answer and blocking design are complete
Design blocking now but enable it only if required
open_points.default_guess: Ship the read-only page independently; require a separate State 0 decision before adding blocking.

open_points.subject: R0-95 recipient follow-up
open_points.text: What still holds a value is followed by the owner, by the governance's procedure, after each such change
open_points.question: How is the owner told that follow-up is required, how are the affected recipients and copies identified, and what observable record proves that correction or erasure was completed?
options: A governance checklist initiated manually after every change
A Registry-generated task containing affected recipient classes
No tracked workflow; the owner relies on memory
open_points.default_guess: Use a documented, manually initiated checklist keyed by the Registry change and record completion outside Registry.

witness.initial: A personal value exists in an issued document and in a legacy service copy.
events: The owner corrects the value in Registry.
Registry sends no feed or notification.
outcomes: The owner follows a recorded checklist and corrects every remaining copy.
The owner considers later reads sufficient and leaves the legacy copy unchanged.
witness.observer: The customer and the owner reviewing compliance

open_points.subject: R0-95 backup erasure period
open_points.text: Registry's backups lose an erased value within the period A18 states.
open_points.question: What is the actual maximum period, when does it start, and does loss occur through expiry, overwrite, deletion or restoration filtering?
options: Delete every affected backup within a fixed period after erasure
Let backups expire under a fixed rolling-retention period
Keep backups but filter erased values during restoration
open_points.default_guess: Apply fixed rolling backup retention measured from the erasure time, with no affected backup restorable after that maximum.

open_points.subject: R0-96 prohibition on special-category names
open_points.text: data of a special category (GDPR Art. 9), which the platform must not hand to an agent. ... Registry cannot tell what a word means, refuses no name for its content and searches no text for words; a name that breaks the rule does reach the agent.
open_points.question: Is preventing special-category data from reaching an agent a platform guarantee or only a writer policy that may fail, and what control handles a violating name before disclosure?
options: Make it a guarantee and add human or automated review before agent disclosure
State explicitly that it is only an organisational writer rule
Remove room names and aliases from the agent projection
open_points.default_guess: Remove unreviewed room names and aliases from the agent projection unless a reliable approval step marks them safe.

witness.initial: A project is visible to an agent session and has a room named "bathroom for the wheelchair".
events: The owner or agent writes the room name.
The agent reads the project projection.
outcomes: The platform withholds or rejects the special-category name because it must not hand it to an agent.
Registry accepts the name and returns it to the agent because content is not checked.
witness.observer: The agent, its AI provider and the affected customer

open_points.subject: R0-96 writer instructions before manifest change
open_points.text: until then the rule binds the owner, and the agent through the governance's instructions to it.
open_points.question: Who injects the governance instruction into every agent session before the manifest description is changed, how is its presence verified, and what happens when it is absent or ignored?
options: Kernel supplies a mandatory versioned instruction to every run
The owner manually instructs each agent session
Agent writes are disabled until the manifest carries the rule
open_points.default_guess: Kernel must attach a versioned mandatory instruction to every run and refuse the write binding if it is unavailable.

open_points.subject: R0-97 refused-attempt counters
open_points.text: Registry counts refused attempts in memory from its start and shows them to the owner on the first page after sign-in, with the instant of the start and of the latest of each kind
open_points.question: What increments each counter, whether overlapping refusals increment one or several kinds, whether a lockout event and its refused sign-ins are counted separately, and whether viewing resets or acknowledges anything?
options: Assign every refusal to exactly one mutually exclusive kind and never reset on viewing
Increment every applicable counter and never reset on viewing
Reset counters after the owner views them
open_points.default_guess: Use mutually exclusive precedence-ordered categories; viewing does not reset them, and only a restart does.

witness.initial: The sign-in lockout threshold has been reached.
events: The same caller submits three more wrong credentials during lockout.
The owner later signs in and views the counters.
outcomes: The page shows one lockout and three refused sign-ins.
The page shows four lockouts, or only the original lockout, depending on how attempts are classified.
witness.observer: The owner assessing a possible breach

open_points.subject: R0-97 security-event page delivery
open_points.text: After the first release is assembled, with the changes R0-93, R0-94 and R0-96 planned, Registry counts refused attempts
open_points.question: Is counting contingent on all three named changes, what precise release must include it, and are attempts before that release intentionally unobservable?
options: Include counting in the first production release
Deliver counting only together with all named post-assembly changes
Give each change an independent release decision
open_points.default_guess: Treat counting as an independent mandatory change in the next release after initial assembly.

open_points.subject: R0-97 durable security log trigger
open_points.text: A durable log of security events ... is reconsidered — by a new owner decision here — when Registry gains a second human principal who signs in to it, or a surface reachable other than through the owner's VPN and the WireGuard channel
open_points.question: What exact topology or principal change triggers reconsideration, must the durable log exist before that change becomes admissible, and what events and retention would it cover?
options: Require the durable log before either trigger is deployed
Allow the trigger and decide logging afterward
Never add a durable log without a separately identified risk finding
open_points.default_guess: Make the durable log a prerequisite for deploying either triggering change.

open_points.subject: R0-98 DPIA screening result
open_points.text: On these facts the screening's likely conclusion is that a DPIA is not required
open_points.question: What is the actual screening conclusion, who is authorised to make it, where is it recorded, and what happens if the conclusion is instead that a DPIA is required?
options: Record a final conclusion that no DPIA is required
Require a DPIA before further processing
Permit processing while a required DPIA is prepared
open_points.default_guess: Do not treat the likely conclusion as final; record the completed screening and require a DPIA before any newly identified high-risk processing.

open_points.subject: R0-98 legacy objects-folder cleanup
open_points.text: It holds once the owner's earlier machine no longer gives the agent the objects folder (the cleanup step of the home server's move).
open_points.question: Who performs the cleanup, what exact access and copies must be removed, how is completion verified, and may production start or import complete before it succeeds?
options: Make verified cleanup a prerequisite to production start and import
Allow import first but block agent processing until verified cleanup
Run both concurrently with no technical gate
open_points.default_guess: Allow the risk-lowering import but block agent processing of affected data until cleanup is verified.

witness.initial: The legacy instance and its objects folder remain accessible to the agent.
events: Production Registry starts and imports the projects.
The screening is recorded using the assumption that photos do not reach the agent.
outcomes: Agent processing is blocked until the legacy access is removed.
The agent continues to access legacy photos while the new Registry is operating.
witness.observer: The owner, the agent and data subjects visible in the photos

open_points.subject: R0-98 effect of import on agent access
open_points.text: The import moves it into one protected home, out of every agent's reach
open_points.question: Does importing itself remove or disable every legacy copy and access path, or does that require the separate cleanup and retirement actions?
options: Import atomically disables all legacy access
Import only copies data; cleanup later removes legacy access
Agent access is blocked independently before import
open_points.default_guess: State that import only copies data and require a separate verified cleanup to put every copy out of the agent's reach.

witness.initial: The VPS data is imported while the earlier machine still exposes its objects folder to the agent.
events: The owner completes the Registry import.
No cleanup has yet occurred.
outcomes: The data is out of every agent's reach as the import claim states.
The agent can still reach the legacy copy until the separate cleanup step.
witness.observer: The agent and the owner performing the migration

open_points.subject: R0-99 standing approval in collection maps
open_points.text: The governance's rule is that no standing approval is given to a node that writes to Registry inside a map over a collection.
open_points.question: Who detects that a node executes inside a collection map, who refuses a prohibited standing approval, and what happens if the owner grants one despite the governance rule?
options: Kernel technically refuses such standing approvals
The owner interface warns but permits them
It remains an organisational rule with no runtime enforcement
open_points.default_guess: Kernel should refuse creation or use of a standing approval for any Registry-writing node in a collection map.

witness.initial: A flow maps an add-room node over 500 generated room descriptions.
events: The owner gives the flow version a standing approval for that node.
The flow runs once.
outcomes: Kernel rejects the standing approval or pauses for every exact room request.
Kernel accepts the standing approval and creates all 500 rooms without further approval.
witness.observer: The owner and users viewing the project

open_points.subject: blocking ownership
open_points.text: blocking under LOPDGDD Art. 32 (R0-91) ... [is] kept as platform-wide governance ... outside this case
open_points.question: If R0-94 later adds blocking to Registry, which parts remain governance and which concrete state, actions, outputs and destruction behavior become Registry responsibilities?
options: Only the legal policy is governance; Registry implements the mechanism
Both policy and mechanism remain outside Registry
Registry stores no blocked values and delegates them to another named service
open_points.default_guess: Keep the legal determination in governance but require a new State 0 decision to define any Registry mechanism.

open_points.subject: closure status of R0-91 to R0-99
open_points.text: None open. ... R0-91 to R0-99 (2026-11-23) answer Q1 to Q9 of the data-protection requirements matrix.
open_points.question: How can these questions be closed while the same decisions leave Kernel correlation, blocking scope and design, post-release operations, durable logging and the DPIA conclusion to later decisions?
options: List each remaining question as open
Remove the deferred promises and keep only current behavior
Declare each item explicitly carried to a named later state with a binding contract
open_points.default_guess: List the unresolved product choices as open until new owner decisions close them.

witness.initial: A later-state designer reads State 0 after R0-91 to R0-99.
events: The designer sees "None open".
The designer must implement trace correlation, retention review and security counting.
outcomes: The designer treats the deferred passages as binding future features and invents their contracts.
The designer treats them as non-adopted candidates and omits them.
witness.observer: The owner and users of the later implementation
